attrs.evidence: R6.1 measured that `active_unresolved` and `strict` produce identical labels on the real corpus and declined to build a distinguishing case, calling it manufacturing a witness. GPT-5.6's audit says that conflated two things and it is right. A POSITIVE CONTROL asks whether the implementation distinguishes the semantics it claims to; it is not evidence that a production argument has that shape. This artifact demands controls everywhere else — §5's `consume` controls exist precisely so that a rule refusing everything cannot pass for a rule refusing this one — and the same standard applies to a semantics. §5b2 exhibits a terminated-only framework where `active_unresolved` leaves the argument standing and `strict` defeats it. ASR-TERMINATOR-UNOBSERVABLE remains the separate measurement that no CURRENT REAL record does. Both are true and the artifact carries both.
attrs.prior_art: GPT-5.6's audit of INV-R6.1 — the one item where it overruled R6.1's reasoning rather than extending it.
attrs.statement: Every declared assurance reading is exhibited distinguishing what it claims to distinguish, on a synthetic framework, independently of whether any real record currently exhibits that shape.
